verdict.rationale: Ramp documents background automation in two forms. First, native autonomous behaviors: rules-based approval and routing workflows, auto-approval of in-policy spend, real-time anomaly scanning by Ramp agents, automatic reminders, and automatic hotel rebooking. Second, custom agent automation: the CLI targets scripted/scheduled workflows (--agent JSON output, --no-input for CI, client-credentials login with no browser), agent keys offer long-running access for scheduled background agents, and webhooks provide event triggers. missing for 10: a first-party hosted scheduler/runtime for custom automations (users must host and schedule agents themselves), documentation of a general-purpose automation builder beyond approval routing rules, independent or hands-on corroboration of background runs.
